competences: The learner explains Jesus' Beatitudes as teachings about Christian happiness.
The learner identifies the people Jesus called blessed and the promises made to them.
languageCompetence: Learners pronounce, read and spell Beatitudes, humble, merciful, mourn, persecution and righteousness.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should be able to identify at least four groups Jesus called blessed.
By the end of the lesson learners should state the promises Jesus gave to humble, merciful and persecuted people.
priorKnowledge: Learners have studied the meaning and examples of discipleship in the previous CRE period.
materials: P5 CRE reference notes on Jesus' teachings
references: P.5 R.E Lesson Notes Term III

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the meaning of discipleship and asks "4. How will people benefit from being humble?". They introduce the teaching of Jesus in Matthew 5 and connect the lesson with humility and mercy.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall examples of discipleship, answer the first question and share what they know about Christian happiness.

steps.content: Jesus taught his disciples about happiness in Matthew 5:1–11. Jesus called blessed the people who live by God's will. The Beatitudes teach humility, mercy and peacemaking. People should desire to do what God requires. Disciples should copy the character and example of Jesus.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the sourced promises under "Jesus' teaching about happiness" using the points "Jesus taught his disciples about happiness in Matthew 5:1–11. Jesus called blessed the people who live by God's will." They assess understanding with "5. Outline any three Jesus teaching on discipleship." and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the beatitude-related points, explain the promised rewards and answer the original questions orally.

steps.stage: Development: People who receive the kingdom of heaven
steps.content: The spiritually poor are promised the kingdom of heaven. Those who seek God should recognise their spiritual needs. People persecuted for righteousness are promised God's kingdom. Followers of Jesus should show courage during persecution. Disciples should remain obedient when facing difficulties.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the sourced promises under "People who receive the kingdom of heaven" using the points "The spiritually poor are promised the kingdom of heaven. Those who seek God should recognise their spiritual needs." They assess understanding with "6. How will God reward the following:-" and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the beatitude-related points, explain the promised rewards and answer the original questions orally.

steps.stage: Development: Promises to the humble and merciful
steps.content: God will comfort people who mourn. Humble people will receive what God has promised. God will show mercy to people who show mercy. Those desiring righteousness will be fully satisfied. Pure-hearted people are promised that they will see God. People who work for peace will be called God's children.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the sourced promises under "Promises to the humble and merciful" using the points "God will comfort people who mourn. Humble people will receive what God has promised." They assess understanding with "7. According to Jesus’ teaching, which four groups of people are to be happy?" and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the beatitude-related points, explain the promised rewards and answer the original questions orally.

steps.stage: Development: Lessons Christians learn from the Beatitudes
steps.content: Christians should be merciful to other people. Christians should make peace with their neighbours. Christians should remain humble before God. Christians should seek to do what God requires. Christians should show courage during persecution. Forgiveness and obedience are examples of true discipleship. Christians should not abandon their faith during suffering.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the sourced promises under "Lessons Christians learn from the Beatitudes" using the points "Christians should be merciful to other people. Christians should make peace with their neighbours." They assess understanding with "3. State two examples of discipleship. ." and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the beatitude-related points, explain the promised rewards and answer the original questions orally.

steps.content: 4. How will people benefit from being humble? | 5. Outline any three Jesus teaching on discipleship. | 6. How will God reward the following:- | 7. According to Jesus’ teaching, which four groups of people are to be happy? | 3. State two examples of discipleship. .
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives learners the sourced questions about Jesus' teaching, beginning with "4. How will people benefit from being humble?" and "5. Outline any three Jesus teaching on discipleship.". They monitor answers, assist with matching promises and check work against the notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the exercise questions individually, recall Christian virtues and correct any incomplete or wrong answers.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the promises of the Beatitudes and asks "7. According to Jesus’ teaching, which four groups of people are to be happy?" and "3. State two examples of discipleship. .". They confirm that the original passages support the responses and set revision homework.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners name a group Jesus called happy and state a virtue before recording the homework question.

assessment: Ask the original questions "4. How will people benefit from being humble?", "5. Outline any three Jesus teaching on discipleship.", and "7. According to Jesus’ teaching, which four groups of people are to be happy?" and mark written work using the beatitudes in the reference notes.
homework: Complete the sourced exercise question "7. According to Jesus’ teaching, which four groups of people are to be happy?"
